result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

args.description: Corvid Retail requested a $2,500 outage credit (DOC-0202, email 2026-03-30) but this is NOT supported by contract terms or verified uptime data. Per Corvid Retail's Subscription Agreement (DOC-0001), SLA credit (10% of monthly fee = $1,150) only applies if monthly uptime is below 99.5%. The March 2026 SRE uptime report (DOC-0211, final, signed off) shows Corvid Retail (us-central) at 99.94% uptime - above the 99.5% threshold, so no SLA breach occurred and no credit is contractually due. Per policy (DOC-0008 Β§7), SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data. Recommend controller review and customer response declining the credit with reference to the uptime report; no journal entry posted.

args.text:
MARCH 2026 US BILLING ADJUSTMENTS - SUMMARY

Reviewed all US customer contracts (Acme Logistics, Beacon Health, Corvid Retail, Evergreen Bank, Fairview Labs) against the March 2026 final usage report (DOC-0210) and the March 2026 final SRE uptime report (DOC-0211) before booking anything.

1) USAGE OVERAGE - Acme Logistics (JE-00304, posted)
   - Order Form 3 (DOC-0003): 1,000,000 API calls included/month; overage billed in arrears at $0.004/call.
   - March usage: 1,284,000 calls -> 284,000 over -> $1,136.00 overage.
   - Not yet invoiced at month-end (invoiced early April per historical pattern), so recorded as earned-but-unbilled usage revenue: Dr 1300 Unbilled Receivables $1,136.00 / Cr 4100 Usage Revenue $1,136.00.
   - Support attached: DOC-0003 (contract), DOC-0210 (usage report).
   - No other US customer has a usage-based/overage contract, so no other overage billings were required.

2) SLA CREDIT - Beacon Health (JE-00305, posted)
   - Subscription Agreement (DOC-0002): credit of 10% of monthly fee if uptime < 99.5%, applied against receivable balance.
   - March uptime (us-west): 99.31% (incident INC-2291, 5h02m outage on 3/11) - SLA breached.
   - Credit = 10% x $8,000 = $800.00: Dr 4000 Subscription Revenue $800.00 / Cr 1100 Accounts Receivable $800.00.
   - Support attached: DOC-0002 (contract), DOC-0211 (uptime report). (Note: Beacon's March invoice was already fully collected 3/19; the credit leaves a $800 credit balance on their account to be applied to the next invoice or refunded per AR team follow-up.)

3) SLA CREDIT REQUEST DECLINED / FLAGGED - Corvid Retail (EXC-001, flagged, not posted)
   - Customer emailed 3/30 requesting a $2,500 outage credit (DOC-0202).
   - Corvid's contract (DOC-0001) only entitles a credit if uptime < 99.5% (10% of $11,500 = $1,150 would be the contractual amount, not the $2,500 requested).
   - March uptime for Corvid Retail (us-central) per the final SRE report was 99.94% - above the SLA threshold. No breach occurred, so no credit is contractually due under any calculation.
   - Flagged to controller for review/customer communication rather than posted, per policy of not forcing entries without support.

4) OTHER CUSTOMERS CHECKED, NO ACTION NEEDED
   - Acme Logistics own SLA (99.97% uptime) and Evergreen Bank (99.97%) and Fairview Labs (99.99%) all met their uptime commitments in March; Evergreen Bank and Fairview Labs also have no SLA credit clause on file. No credits due.

Both posted entries are under the $10,000 single-accountant posting threshold (DOC-0008 Β§1) and have supporting documentation attached (Β§2). No entry was posted to force a match with the unsupported Corvid Retail request.
